archetype: Melee STR pirate built on a skill-linking system: attacks chain into one another with no end-lag as long as you alternate inputs, and the core damage loop is alternating two main attacks. Sustained DPM class with very high mobility and strong boss uptime tools rather than one large burst window, though 6th job added a stronger 2 minute burst, an over-shield and an Origin skill. Party utility is limited to an attack speed buff.

linkSkill.name: Cygnus Blessing
linkSkill.effect: Shared Cygnus Knights link skill. Grants flat Attack Power and Magic ATT plus Abnormal Status Resistance and All Elemental Resistance. Stacks up to 5 times, once per unique Cygnus Knights job character on the world.
linkSkill.levels: maplestorywiki.net Thunder_Breaker/Skills: Lv1 = ATT and MATT +7, Abnormal Status Resistance +1, All Elemental Resistance +1%; max level = ATT and MATT +35, Abnormal Status Resistance +22, All Elemental Resistance +22%. Grandis Library states the same max values and adds that Mihile is excluded from the 5-character stack.

priority.why: The class doc's ordering reads 'Annihilate, Thunderbolt, and Gale/Typhoon Boost Nodes equally' as the step after the common nodes. mastermysty's cross-class table independently names Thunderbolt / Annihilate / Gale as Thunder Breaker's primary trio. maplestorywiki confirms these are three separate enhancement cores (Core 1, Core 2, Core 3) that can therefore share one trio slot.
priority.consensusNote: Two independent sources agree on the trio MEMBERSHIP (class doc and mastermysty). The instruction to level the three EQUALLY rather than in sequence is class-doc only. mastermysty's data is dated 2024-05-14 and predates the v269 boost node regrouping, so its agreement is weaker than its independence suggests. maplestorywiki is counted as game data for the grouping, not as a third judgement.

priority.consensusNote: Single source. Name validated against maplestorywiki.

priority.why: Sixth line of the class doc's ordering; a low-cooldown attack used off cooldown during normal DPM.
priority.consensusNote: Single source. Name validated against maplestorywiki.

It is actively CONTRADICTED by the other source in the same family: Grandis Library files Tidal Crash / Sea Wave / Shark Sweep under OTHER, its lowest tier, and says to prioritise PRIMARY and SECONDARY nodes for upgrades - i.e. Grandis says this node is not worth building. trios.trio: Annihilate Boost + Thunderbolt Boost + Gale Boost
trios.consensusNote: Named by the 2026 class doc and independently by mastermysty's node table. Two independent sources, but mastermysty's underlying data is 2024-05-14 and pre-regrouping.

trios.consensusNote: Appears only in mastermysty's 2024 table, whose data predates the v269 boost node regrouping. Both 2026 sources disagree: the class doc's ordering ends at the Tidal Crash / Sea Wave / Shark Sweep node and never mentions an Ascension trio, and Grandis Library files Ascension and Thunder under OTHER. Retained as a recorded position, not a recommendation. See conflicts[].

vMatrix.notes: Boost node groupings as published by maplestorywiki (game data, no judgement attached), re-read verbatim 2026-09-12 and reproduced by Grandis Library: Core 1 = Annihilate Boost; Core 2 = Thunderbolt Boost; Core 3 = Gale Boost and Deep Rising Boost; Core 4 = Tidal Crash Boost, Sea Wave Boost, Shark Sweep Boost; Core 5 = Thunder Boost and Ascension Boost; Core 6 = Flash Boost and Lightning Punch Boost. Boost node level cap is 60. GRANDIS LIBRARY TIERING, CORRECTED 2026-09-12: PRIMARY = Annihilate and Thunderbolt (Grandis' stated reason is that these nodes unlock the 6th job HEXA Masteries and carry frequently-used skills); SECONDARY = Gale, Typhoon and Deep Rising (Grandis notes it does not unlock a HEXA Mastery but still sees regular use); OTHER = Tidal Crash, Sea Wave, Shark Sweep, Ascension, Thunder, Flash and Lightning Punch. Grandis recommends prioritising PRIMARY and SECONDARY for upgrades. An earlier revision of this file wrongly placed Tidal Crash / Sea Wave / Shark Sweep in SECONDARY, which turned a real disagreement with the class doc into false agreement; that is fixed and the disagreement is now recorded in conflicts[]. maplestorywiki lists final damage per level by skill: Lightning Punch and Flash boosts highest at 7% per level, Shark Sweep / Tidal Crash / Sea Wave at 5%, Ascension / Thunder at 3%, and Gale / Annihilate / Thunderbolt / Deep Rising lowest at 2% but with extra effects at levels 20 and 40 (max targets, ignore DEF, critical rate). Sources: https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Thunder_Breaker/Skills and https://grandislibrary.com/cygnus-knights/thunder-breaker

The class doc reproduces the same thing as a single 'HEXA Matrix Leveling Guide' image, annotated '*Updated to include HEXA Phalanx Charge'.

order.step: HEXA Stat line value order for Thunder Breaker: ATT, then flat STR, then Critical Damage, then Boss Damage, then Damage, then Ignore DEF. With only three HEXA Stat nodes available in v.271, a player is working with ATT, flat STR and Critical Damage only.

hexa.orderNote: These five entries are independent statements about 6th job investment, not a ranked sequence. Array position carries no priority meaning here. The actual node-by-node order is the gap described in entry 1 and is NOT recorded in this file.
hexa.notes: Node inventory re-validated against maplestorywiki 2026-09-12 so nothing here is invented. Skill Nodes: Core 1 (Origin) = Thunder Wall Sea Wave; Core 2 (Ascent) = Annihilating Rush. Mastery Nodes: Core 1 = HEXA Annihilate (also raises Thunder Bolt); Core 2 = HEXA Thunderbolt; Core 3 = HEXA Typhoon and HEXA Deep Rising; Core 4 = HEXA Sea Wave (also raises Deep Reinforcement). HEXA Enhancement (boost) nodes, confirmed as exactly four on the wiki: Lightning Cascade Boost, Shark Torpedo Boost, Lightning God Spear Strike Boost, Lightning Spear Multistrike Boost - all level requirement 260, master level 30, final damage rising linearly with jumps at levels 10, 20 and 30. A HEXA enhancement for Phalanx Charge was added in v.271 and is still absent from the maplestorywiki HEXA Enhancements table as re-read on 2026-09-12; the class doc records it as a level 30 skill and quotes MapleScouter figures of roughly +0.42% final damage at level 1, +1.18% at 10, +2.00% at 20 and +2.86% at 30 - those figures are class-doc-only and second-hand. HEXA Stat node unlocks per the class doc: node I at Lv 260 for 5 Sol Erda and 10 fragments, node II at Lv 265 for 10 Sol Erda and 200 fragments, node III at Lv 270 for 15 Sol Erda and 350 fragments; resets cost 10m, 20m and 35m mesos respectively. The doc also flags a KMS change (v.1.2.417 MapleStory Overdrive, 2026-07-31) adding a third HEXA skill core, Sea Emperor Smash, worth roughly 2.5-3% final damage at level 30 - not in GMS as of v.271, so any HEXA order will shift when it arrives. Sources: https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Thunder_Breaker/Skills and https://docs.google.com/document/d/149bORdBFd99UJSFbza52zv5AJw4VfB4kvqC5p4K-97g/mobilebasic
hexa.noteOnCharacterLevel154: At Lv 154 none of this is reachable yet - 5th job and the V Matrix begin at 200, 6th job and the HEXA Matrix at 260. The actionable items at this level are the hyper skill passives (from Lv 140) and hyper stats.

hyperStats.priorityOrderNote: Deliberately null, not an empty or unordered list. No source read publishes a Thunder Breaker hyper stat ranking, so this file stores no ordered array that downstream code could read as one. Re-confirmed 2026-09-12: a case-insensitive search for 'hyper stat' returns zero hits in the class doc and zero on the Grandis Library Thunder Breaker page.
hyperStats.notes: NOT SOURCED. The Thunder Breaker class doc has no hyper stat section at all, and Grandis Library publishes no hyper stat allocation for any class. No independent Thunder Breaker hyper stat ranking was found. Two sourced facts bear on it. (1) Thunder Breaker gains +40% critical rate and +30% critical damage from its own passives and 0% boss damage from passives (Grandis Library base-stats-from-skills table), which is why boss damage has to be bought from elsewhere. (2) CORRECTED 2026-09-12: the class doc's Links section says, verbatim, 'If you're early in the game and lacking crit rate, feel free to swap out Xenon link for Lynn/Phantom link as needed.' - that is, the Xenon link is the one REMOVED and Lynn or Phantom are swapped IN when critical rate is short. An earlier revision of this file stated the reverse (that the doc's answer to low crit rate was the Xenon link); that was a citation inversion, no source says it, and Xenon's link skill is an all-stat percentage rather than critical rate. TWO THINGS THAT MUST NOT BE RELABELLED AS HYPER STATS: the doc's Legion Grid ranking (critical rate as needed, then boss damage, critical damage, ignore DEF, STR, attack power, buff duration only when running the Angelic Buster link, DEX) is a LEGION recommendation; and the ATT > flat STR > Crit Dmg > Boss Dmg > Damage > IED ordering in hexa.order is a HEXA STAT recommendation. Neither is a hyper stat list. The community's operative answer to hyper stat priority is MathBro's per-character optimizer at https://brendonmay.github.io/hyperCalculator/, not a fixed list. Sources: https://docs.google.com/document/d/149bORdBFd99UJSFbza52zv5AJw4VfB4kvqC5p4K-97g/mobilebasic and https://grandislibrary.com/cygnus-knights/thunder-breaker

The class doc's 'Hyper Skill Passives' list and Grandis Library's hyper passive build both name it, but Grandis' credits block reads 'Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build: Thunder Breaker Discord', so Grandis is restating the same Discord that authors the class doc. maplestorywiki validates that the skill NAME exists in the nine-skill hyper passive pool; it carries no recommendation and is not counted as a judgement source.

hyperSkills.actives_note: No source read gives a recommended hyper ACTIVE loadout for Thunder Breaker. Re-confirmed 2026-09-12: the class doc has a heading 'Hyper Skill Passives' and no active counterpart, and Grandis Library lists only a passive build. Left null deliberately.
hyperSkills.notes: The full hyper passive pool per maplestorywiki, enumerated directly from the page 2026-09-12, is exactly nine: Gale - Reinforce / Spread / Extra Strike, Thunderbolt - Reinforce / Spread / Extra Strike, and Annihilate - Reinforce / Guardbreak / Boss Rush. The five recommended above are drawn from those nine; the four not taken are Gale - Spread, Thunderbolt - Reinforce, Thunderbolt - Spread and Annihilate - Guardbreak, and no source read explains why those four are passed over. Two class hyper skills sit outside the passive pool and matter because the doc's rotation is built on them: Primal Bolt (Lv 140) removes the Gale/Typhoon cooldown for its duration, raises Lightning Elemental's ignore DEF from 45% to 50%, and shortens the cooldowns of Sea Wave, Shark Torpedo and Lightning God Spear Strike while linking; Deep Rising (Lv 160) is a 45 second cooldown invincibility of a few seconds that can be linked into and out of. Sources: https://maplestorywiki.net/w/Thunder_Breaker/Skills and https://docs.google.com/document/d/149bORdBFd99UJSFbza52zv5AJw4VfB4kvqC5p4K-97g/mobilebasic

innerAbility.notes: Attack speed is not listed as an inner ability target for this class by any source read. Grandis Library's base-stat table shows Thunder Breaker reaching attack speed 8 on its own at Lightning Elemental stage 5, with Speed Infusion adding +2 more without breaking the soft cap - which would explain why no source recommends the attack speed line, but no source says so explicitly. Flagged as an INFERENCE, not sourced advice, and it should not be surfaced to a player as a recommendation. Source: https://grandislibrary.com/cygnus-knights/thunder-breaker

gearingNotes: What the class supplies itself, which is what determines where gear, legion and hyper stat points should go (Grandis Library base-stats-from-skills table): weapon multiplier 1.7x; attack speed 8 at Lightning Elemental stage 5 plus +2 from Speed Infusion that does not break the soft cap; weapon mastery 90%; STR +60 and +1 per 2 levels plus 15% of assigned AP; attack +14% and +170 flat (up to +210); critical rate +40%; critical damage +30%; damage +40% base rising to +122% with conditional sources; BOSS DAMAGE +0% from passives; final damage about +49% base rising to +89% conditionally; ignore DEF +45%, up to 50% while Primal Bolt is active. Consequences drawn from those numbers plus the class doc: (1) CORRECTED 2026-09-12 - critical rate is the stat a Thunder Breaker is most likely to be short of early, and the class doc's answer is to SWAP OUT the Xenon link in favour of the Lynn or Phantom link: 'If you're early in the game and lacking crit rate, feel free to swap out Xenon link for Lynn/Phantom link as needed.' An earlier revision of this file inverted that, saying the doc's answer was the Xenon link; it is not, and Xenon's link is an all-stat percentage rather than critical rate; (2) with zero boss damage from passives, boss damage must come from gear, legion, inner ability and hyper stats; (3) the doc's LEGION GRID order is critical rate as needed, then boss damage, critical damage, ignore DEF, STR, attack power, buff duration (only when running the Angelic Buster link), DEX; its LEGION ARTIFACT order is critical rate / boss damage / damage, then ignore DEF / all stats / critical damage, then attack power / buff duration / cooldown skip, with EXP / drop rate / meso obtained as the training alternative - both re-read verbatim 2026-09-12, and neither is a hyper stat list; (4) cooldown-reduction hat: the doc says most Thunder Breakers run a -2 second, 2-line-stat hat while some prefer 3 lines of stat, that cooldown reduction affects Gale/Typhoon, Shark Torpedo, Lightning God Spear Strike and all burst buffs including the skill ring, and that a casual player should keep whichever they roll first; (5) ring choice: as a sustained-DPM class Continuous Ring is better in the abstract, but Ring of Restraint wins on bosses where 100% uptime is impossible such as Kalos or Kaling - the doc notes this becomes moot in a future patch allowing a passive and an active ring together. Sources: https://grandislibrary.com/cygnus-knights/thunder-breaker and https://docs.google.com/document/d/149bORdBFd99UJSFbza52zv5AJw4VfB4kvqC5p4K-97g/mobilebasic

commonMistakes.mistake: Using the in-game macro to combo. It does not work with Thunder Breaker's linking system.
Pressing the same attack twice in a row instead of linking two different skills. Repeating one skill incurs heavy end-lag between casts.
Casting Gale/Typhoon or Shark Torpedo below 5 Lightning Elemental stacks. The doc says to fire both only at max stacks.
Linking Lightning Spear Multistrike into other skills or holding the key down. Its 12 casts are pressed back to back on their own.
Wasting Lightning Brands. A brand applied by HEXA Annihilate is consumed by the next non-Annihilate attack, so Gale/Typhoon and Shark Torpedo should be woven in directly after an Annihilate.
Never upgrading Empress Cygnus's Blessing. Talking to Neinheart in Moonbridge after the questline upgrades it to the Transcendent version, which adds damage reduction for the buff's duration.
Burning fragments rerolling HEXA Stat main stats before the HEXA Matrix is finished.
Mashing harder or faster expecting more attacks. The doc states it does not produce more damage and covers keybinding and wrist-strain mitigation instead.

conflicts.topic: Is the Tidal Crash / Sea Wave / Shark Sweep boost node worth building at all
conflicts.positionA: The class doc's node-starved priority list ends with 'Tidal Crash/Sea Wave/Shark Sweep Boost Node' as the eighth and last boost node worth building.
conflicts.positionB: Grandis Library files Tidal Crash, Sea Wave and Shark Sweep under OTHER, its lowest tier, and recommends prioritising only PRIMARY and SECONDARY nodes for upgrades - so it does not rate this node worth building.
conflicts.status: contested, not resolved. ADDED 2026-09-12: an earlier revision of this file recorded Grandis as placing this node in SECONDARY, which made the two sources look like they agreed. Grandis does not; the tier is OTHER. Note the two are nominally the same source family, so this is a divergence inside the Thunder Breaker Discord lineage, possibly just the two-patch gap between Grandis' v269 stamp and the doc's v.271 body.

conflicts.status: contested but shallow - both trace to the same Thunder Breaker Discord, and Grandis' tiering is explicitly about which nodes unlock HEXA Masteries rather than a levelling sequence, so the two may not actually disagree. Recorded rather than resolved.

evidenceNote: HONEST SOURCING VERDICT, re-stated after the 2026-09-12 resolution pass. Three independent sources were reached, but only two of them carry judgement, and one of those two is nearly two years old. The judgement lanes are (1) the Thunder Breaker Discord family - the C0nfeddie class doc, that Discord's 2026-09-04 infographics, and Grandis Library, which credits the Discord by name for inner ability, hyper passives and boost nodes and therefore does NOT count as a second opinion - and (2) mastermysty's 2024-11-21 node table. The third independent source, maplestorywiki, is facts only and is used here to validate every node and skill name so nothing in this file is invented; it is never counted toward sourceCount on a judgement claim. That is why almost every endgame claim in this file is labelled weak with sourceCount 1: it is accurate, not lazy. Only the primary boost node trio reaches moderate, on two independent sources. NOTHING in this file is labelled strong: the one claim that previously was - that the 6th job order exists solely as community infographics - was downgraded to weak on 2026-09-12 because its two apparent sources are the same Discord lineage and the 3-independent-source bar was not met. Reddit could not be read in this environment and NamuWiki's Striker page was blocked by Cloudflare, so the KMS cross-check is missing; no YouTube-creator pass was possible. The two biggest remaining gaps, both recorded as gaps rather than filled with guesses: no hyper stat ranking exists for this class anywhere public (hyperStats.priority is null), and the HEXA investment order exists only as an unlabelled image (hexa.order records the shape, not the node identities).

contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm.

resolutionPass.scope: Endgame only: vMatrix, hexa, hyperSkills, hyperStats, innerAbility. Every cited page was re-opened and the disputed text re-read verbatim. No new sources were sought.
resolutionPass.method: The Grandis Library page and the class doc were fetched as raw HTML with a browser user agent and searched directly, rather than read as rendered summaries - which is how the infographic date defect was resolved.

resolved.defect: The Xenon link claim is an inversion of the source. The class doc says 'If you're early in the game and lacking crit rate, feel free to swap out Xenon link for Lynn/Phantom link as needed' - Xenon is removed, Lynn/Phantom supply crit rate. The file states the reverse in hyperStats.notes and gearingNotes item 1. Independently wrong too: Xenon's link is all-stat %, not critical rate.
resolved.verdict: CONFIRMED - the defect was real. CORRECTED.
resolved.evidence: Class doc re-fetched 2026-09-12 and the Links section read verbatim: 'If you're early in the game and lacking crit rate, feel free to swap out Xenon link for Lynn/Phantom link as needed.' That is the only mention of Xenon, Lynn or Phantom anywhere in the document.
resolved.action: Rewrote hyperStats.notes and gearingNotes consequence (1) to state the correct direction - Xenon is the link swapped OUT, Lynn or Phantom swapped IN - and left an explicit note in both places that the earlier revision inverted it, so the error cannot silently return.

resolved.defect: vMatrix.notes assigns the Tidal Crash / Sea Wave / Shark Sweep node to Grandis Library's SECONDARY tier. Grandis tiers it OTHER; only Gale/Typhoon/Deep Rising is SECONDARY. The file also quotes Grandis' rule that Primary and Secondary are the ones worth upgrading - so corrected, Grandis says this node is NOT worth building while the class doc ranks it 8th. A real conflict was converted into agreement and left out of conflicts[].
resolved.verdict: CONFIRMED - the defect was real. CORRECTED.
resolved.evidence: Grandis Library Thunder Breaker page re-read 2026-09-12. PRIMARY = Annihilate, Thunderbolt (reason given: these unlock 6th job HEXA Masteries and see frequent use). SECONDARY = Gale, Typhoon, Deep Rising (does not unlock a HEXA Mastery but still sees regular use). OTHER = Tidal Crash, Sea Wave, Shark Sweep, Ascension, Thunder, Flash, Lightning Punch. The page recommends prioritising PRIMARY and SECONDARY for upgrades.
resolved.action: Corrected the tier assignment in vMatrix.notes; changed the Tidal Crash node's priority entry from 'grouping corroborated by Grandis' to 'contested, Grandis actively deprioritises it', removed Grandis from that entry's sources[] and moved it to a new contradictedBy[] field, cut sourceCount to 1; added a new first entry to conflicts[] recording the disagreement. The node itself is KEPT because the class doc really does rank it eighth - only the false corroboration was removed.

resolved.defect: The 2026-09-04 infographic date is asserted four times as metadata 'recorded by Grandis Library alongside the image'. Two separate fetches of the Grandis page report no dates anywhere on the page beyond the GMS Ver. 269 stamp, and the PNG carries no printed date. Unsupported, and load-bearing.
resolved.verdict: REFUTED - the original claim is sound. CONFIRMED, no content change.
resolved.evidence: The date is real but is not rendered as visible page text, which is why text-extraction reads of the page miss it. Fetching https://grandislibrary.com/cygnus-knights/thunder-breaker as raw HTML on 2026-09-12 returns an embedded infographics array whose first entry is src 'thunder-breaker/thunder-breaker-6th-job-fragments.png', title '6th Job (Fragments Efficient)', credit 'Thunder Breaker Discord', date '2026-09-04', with the identical shape for the energy-efficient sibling. The same fetch confirms the credits entry 'Inner Ability + Hyper Passive Build + Boost Nodes Build' / 'Thunder Breaker Discord' that this file relies on for its independence accounting.
resolved.action: No claim changed. Added a note in hexa.order and in sources[] recording WHERE the date lives and why a rendered read of the page misses it, so this defect is not raised a fourth time.

clearedOnInspection: Boost node core groupings in vMatrix.notes (Core 1 Annihilate; Core 2 Thunderbolt; Core 3 Gale + Deep Rising; Core 4 Tidal Crash + Sea Wave + Shark Sweep; Core 5 Thunder + Ascension; Core 6 Flash + Lightning Punch) - re-read directly off maplestorywiki 2026-09-12, exact match, level cap 60 confirmed.

The eight-step V matrix priority ORDER - re-read verbatim off the class doc 2026-09-12 and it matches this file's array element for element, including the 'Lvl 25 Erda Nova minimum (for 120s cd bind)' line. The ordered array shape is therefore justified and is now flagged as such.

All five hyper passive names, and the claim that the full pool is nine - enumerated directly off maplestorywiki 2026-09-12: Gale Reinforce/Spread/Extra Strike, Thunderbolt Reinforce/Spread/Extra Strike, Annihilate Reinforce/Guardbreak/Boss Rush. No extraction artifacts: every skill and node name in the endgame sections of this file exists in a source that was reached.
hyperSkills.actives being null - the class doc's only hyper heading is 'Hyper Skill Passives' and Grandis lists a passive build only.
hyperStats.priority being null - a case-insensitive search for 'hyper stat' returns zero hits in both the class doc and the Grandis page. The section correctly stores no ordered array.
The HEXA Stat ordering ATT > flat STR > Crit Dmg > Boss Dmg > Damage > IED, and the three-node limitation - both quoted verbatim from the class doc 2026-09-12.

The four HEXA enhancement cores (Lightning Cascade, Shark Torpedo, Lightning God Spear Strike, Lightning Spear Multistrike Boost) and the absence of a Phalanx Charge HEXA enhancement from maplestorywiki - confirmed 2026-09-12.
mastermysty's Thunder Breaker rows (primary Thunderbolt/Annihilate/Gale, secondary Ascension/Deep Rising/Tidal Crash) and its 2024-11-21 / 2024-05-14 dating - re-read 2026-09-12.
